name: reveal

changes.note: Fix: the reduced-motion block now repeats every trigger selector. `[data-ui="reveal"]` alone (0,1,0) lost to the load and scroll triggers (0,2,0 to 0,4,0), so reveals still played under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

description: Entrance choreography for any content: seven effects, three triggers (on load, scrubbed by scroll, or released by a state), and a staggered mode that brings a group's children in one after another. Pure CSS — a view timeline where supported, a load entrance where not — and every distance, duration and easing is a motion token a theme can re-point.

stagger.description: Move the entrance from the root to its direct children: each child arrives --motion-stagger after the sibling before it. Twelve steps are counted; children past the twelfth arrive with it.

--reveal-delay.description: Time before the entrance starts (custom property). Added to the stagger offset. Ignored by the scroll trigger, where the scrollbar is the clock.

--reveal-duration.description: Length of the entrance for this instance (custom property).

--reveal-ease.description: Easing of the entrance for this instance (custom property). Pass an easing token, e.g. var(--ease-spring).

--reveal-distance.description: How far rise, fall and the two slides travel (custom property).

--reveal-range-start.description: Scroll trigger only: how far into the viewport's entry edge the element is when the entrance begins (custom property, a percentage of the entry range).

--reveal-range-end.description: Scroll trigger only: the point of the entry range at which the entrance is complete (custom property).

a11y.notes: Motion only: a reveal adds no role, no name and no focus stop, and never removes its content from the accessibility tree. Under prefers-reduced-motion and in print every trigger resolves to the final state, including a hidden state a script has not released.

templates.html_on_view: {children}

notes: A reveal wraps; it never styles what it wraps. Put the grid, stack or card inside it — or put data-ui="reveal" on a wrapper around a single component. An element cannot be two components, so a reveal is always its own element.

data-trigger="scroll" needs no script: it is a view timeline, scrubbed by the scrollbar, and it reverses when the element leaves the way it came. For an entrance that plays ONCE on a clock when the element is first seen, load the faqir-intersect plugin and use the html_on_view template — the page writes data-state, the stylesheet does the rest.

While an entrance is running the element (or, with data-stagger, each child) carries a transform, so it is the containing block for fixed descendants. Keep sticky headers and fixed overlays outside a reveal.
Stagger order is source order. Reorder the children to reorder the entrance.
